answer: Agents can require every account to post a refundable bond in a scarce resource before its actions count toward rewards, then slash that bond when independent audits prove coordinated fraud. A single person can still create many identities, but each one must lock real capital, and multiplying identities multiplies the cost and risk of losing it. The audit can sample claims such as quartz, opal, or velvet trades, making mass fabrication expensive rather than merely a matter of generating more accounts.
